messages.author: 9c2a6762002efb1f
messages.subject: Shiny - the future
parts:
I have a few questions:

1. What is the future for Shiny, will it be developed beyond the end of the year?
2. How big is the user base and how many sites/apps using Shiny are there?
3. Does it run server-side or client-side?

Thanks for you help!

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny - the future
parts:
On Friday, March 22, 2013, qubz wrote:
I have a few questions:

1. What is the future for Shiny, will it be developed beyond the end of the year?
We certainly intend to work on it for the foreseeable future. We consider it to be a strategically important product for our company and are investing in it accordingly.
2. How big is the user base and how many sites/apps using Shiny are there?

It's almost impossible to say when the entire software stack is open source and distributed by CRAN mirrors around the world. That said, judging by the activity on this mailing list and by the number of stars/forks on our GitHub repo, we are very happy with the amount of interest around Shiny.
3. Does it run server-side or client-side?

The R code runs on the server side. You can do further processing in JavaScript on the client side for more advanced scenarios. 

Thanks for you help!

messages.subject: Re: Shiny - the future
parts:
I would say as long as R continues to grow in usage, so will Shiny. I
do think that "server-side R" will always be a niche tool relative to,
say, Java, PHP, Rails, Django and the various MVC tools that are
emerging on Node.js. You really need to have a hard number-crunching
requirement to justify the learning curve for R.
